title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S a smooth proper curve whose fibres are connected of genus g ≥ 2, with 2 invertible on S. ω denotes the relative canonical sheaf ω_{X/S}. V is the rank-3 bundle with filtration V ≃ ω + O_X + ω^{-1}, essentially the adjoint, sl_2-type bundle attached to the second jet bundle. A projective connection c is a connection ^cD : V → V⊗ω of a fixed shape. In a local uniformizer t it reads ^cD_t(λdt + μ + ν dt^{-1}) = λ'dt² + (μ' − 2λ)dt + (ν' − μ). This is exactly the 'oper' normal form for PGL2.

A global 1-form ω ∈ Γ(X,ω) acts on V by the unipotent gauge automorphism u_ω = exp θ_ω, an element of the unipotent radical of the Borel. The previous page computes the transformed connection u_ω(c) = (u_ω⊗id)∘c∘u_ω^{-1} in a chart. This page records the result: u_ω(c) = c + d^1_{ω/S}(ω), where d^1(ω) is an explicit correction involving 2ω (in the dt-component) and −Dω + ω² (in the dt²-component).

Consequences drawn:
(a) The transformed connection is again in projective-connection (oper) form only if the 'off-normal-form' component vanishes, i.e. 2ω = 0. With 2 invertible this means ω = 0. So no nontrivial unipotent gauge transformation relates two distinct projective connections. Hence different projective connections never yield isomorphic G-bundles with connection through this procedure: the map Conn(X) → M^G(X) is injective on the unipotent-gauge level.
(b) u_ω(c) = c forces ω = 0, so the unipotent part contributes no automorphisms.

Grothendieck then sets up the diagram M_g(X) → M^G(X) ← Conn(X). Here M^G(X) is the moduli of G = PGL2 bundles with (flat) connection, and the source on the left is presumably uniformization data. He asks in the margin whether the objects have automorphisms. His answer is no, by a stronger argument. Suppose there were an automorphism. Then the PGL2-bundle with connection would reduce to an 'affine' (Borel) subgroup. So it would be P(F) for a G-extension 0 → M → F → O_X → 0 with M a horizontal invertible sheaf. Then E ≃ F⊗L.

The next page finishes the argument:
- Taking determinants gives ω ≃ M⊗L².
- deg M = 0 (M carries a connection, in characteristic 0), so deg L = g − 1 > 0.
- The composite ω^{-1} → E → L is a section of L⊗ω, which has negative degree in his convention, so it vanishes.
- Hence L is a quotient of E/ω^{-1} ≅ O, giving deg L = 0, a contradiction.

So the monodromy cannot be reduced to a Borel subgroup. By passing to étale covers (genus stays ≥ 2) it cannot be reduced to a torus normalizer either. This leads to the theorem: the PGL2-local system of any projective connection on a genus ≥ 2 curve (in characteristic 0) admits no reduction to a proper closed subgroup.
errors: Step b) on this page only excludes automorphisms coming from the unipotent radical exp θ_ω. Automorphisms not preserving the Borel/filtration are not covered; Grothendieck himself notices this and supplies the separate degree argument below ('Non, car s'il y en avait...').
The degree argument needs deg M = 0, which uses the existence of a connection on M and characteristic 0 (or at least care in characteristic p). Grothendieck flags 'de car. nulle ?' on the next page.
In the next-page degree computation the sign/twist (L⊗ω^{-1} vs L⊗ω) is written ambiguously, but the conclusion (negative degree, hence vanishing) is correct for the standard oper bundle.

Passing from 'automorphism exists' to 'reduction to a Borel' is asserted quickly. A nontrivial automorphism of a PGL2-local system gives a reduction to its centralizer, which could also be a torus normalizer or finite-type. These are handled on the next page by the étale-cover argument, but the finite primitive subgroups (A4, S4, A5) are not explicitly treated in what is visible.

ideas.what: Action of unipotent gauge transformations exp θ_ω (ω a global 1-form) on projective connections viewed as connections on the filtered rank-3 bundle ω ⊕ O ⊕ ω^{-1}; the oper normal form is rigid (only ω = 0 preserves it when 2 is invertible)
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of oper normal form / opers have trivial unipotent gauge stabilizer; Drinfeld–Sokolov gauge

ideas.what: Map from projective connections to the moduli of PGL2-bundles with connection is injective, and the images have no automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Op_{PGL2}(X) → Loc_{PGL2}(X) is a closed embedding; opers have trivial automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Beilinson–Drinfeld; classically Gunning (1967) for projective structures

ideas.what: Degree argument showing the PGL2-bundle with flat connection attached to a projective connection admits no flat Borel reduction (genus ≥ 2), extended via étale covers to torus normalizers
ideas.modern_name: Irreducibility / Zariski density of monodromy of projective structures (opers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning; Gallo–Kapovich–Marden (2000) for non-elementary monodromy; standard in the oper literature

ideas.what: Relative formulation over a base S with 2 invertible (projective connections on X/S)
ideas.modern_name: Relative opers / projective structures in families, mixed characteristic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller, 1990s) for dormant/indigenous bundles in char p

missed.claim: A purely algebraic, relative-over-S treatment of PGL2-opers ('connexions projectives') is visible here: rigidity of normal form, injectivity into the moduli of G-bundles with connection, absence of automorphisms, and Zariski density of monodromy. It is phrased in a uniformization context (diagram M_g → M^G ← Conn) and likely predates Beilinson–Drinfeld. The results themselves are known, but this is an unrecorded independent Grothendieck treatment of what became oper theory.
missed.quote: u_ω(c) = c + d^1_{ω/S}(ω) si c connexion projective ... il n'y a pas de G-automorphismes des G-fibrés en droites projectives associés à une conn. proj.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck working on algebraic uniformization via opers / indigenous bundles, in the line later developed by Mochizuki and Beilinson–Drinfeld. Mathematically it is routine by today's standards.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (oper rigidity, no automorphisms, irreducible / Zariski-dense monodromy) is standard today. The interest lies in Grothendieck's independent algebraic, relative, 2-invertible formulation within an uniformization programme, which is not recorded in his published texts.
transcription_corrections: 'n'est une connexion projective [-?-] [?] ssi Ωω = 0' likely reads 'n'est une connexion projective que si 2ω = 0' (the obstruction is the −2ω dt term computed on the previous page).
'à fibres de genre [?] connexes de genre g ≥ 2' should read 'à fibres connexes de genre g ≥ 2'.
'le G-fibré serait associé à un G-fibré [?] donc serait isomorphe : un P(F)' plausibly reads 'serait réductible à un G-fibré affine, donc serait isomorphe à un P(F)'.
'Λ M un G-faisceau inv.' likely means 'où M est un G-faisceau inversible'.
'G' throughout is a script letter (a group scheme, here PGL2 or its Borel), not a plain G; 'M_g(X)' may denote the uniformization-type moduli M_g rather than a sheaf on X.
